## 6. Lifecycle semantics

### Vocabulary

10 catalog rows.

| word | where legal | accepts | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@hardDelete` | on a model's field · on a type's field · on a trait's field | — | On a File field: delete the stored object even when the row is only soft-deleted. |
| `@keep` | on a model's field · on a type's field · on a trait's field | — | On a hasMany field of a @@softDelete parent: these children stay live when the parent is soft-deleted, and so does everything below them. |
| `@sealed` | on a model's field · on a type's field · on a trait's field | — | On a hasMany field of a model that declares a @seals move: these children are part of the DOCUMENT, so once the parent seals they may not be created, changed or removed. |
| `@version` | on a model's field · on a trait's field | — | Optimistic concurrency. |
| `@@softDelete` | in a model · in a trait | `[(cascade)]` | Two verbs, and only one of them marks: remove() stamps deletedAt and restore() is the way back, while delete() destroys the row here exactly as it does anywhere else, leaving nothing to restore. |
| `@@transitions` | in a model · in a trait | `(<field>, [<name>:] <from>\|[<from>,…] -> <to> [@gate(N)] [@system] [@seals] [@stamps(col, …, by: col)], …) \| (<field>, declaredBy: Model, scope: <column>)` | A state machine on a CLOSED column — an enum, or a Boolean, which is the two-state machine every schema has (isPrimary, isPublished, isSuspended) and whose two directions are routinely different authorities. |
| `@gate` | on a @@transitions transition | `(<0-9>)` | The model's @@gate at move grain: the level a caller needs to MAKE this move, a floor on top of the model's update level. |
| `@system` | on a @@transitions transition | — | The column's @system at move grain: the move is the APPLICATION's write, where the column is a value the application writes. |
| `@seals` | on a @@transitions transition | — | The move is the moment this row becomes a DOCUMENT. |
| `@stamps` | on a @@transitions transition | `(<column>, …, [by: <column>])` | The move records WHEN it was made: the named DateTime columns get the clock in the move's own UPDATE, the way @updatedAt does, whether the move was made by transition(id, name) or by an update that lands it. |

- `@@softDelete` **`mode`** takes `cascade`

## Host wiring (stays implementation)

The `operate` group. These wire litestone to an app and a runtime, and are listed so that none is lost,
not because a spec would state them.

10 catalog rows.

| word | where legal | accepts | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@override` | on a model's field | — | This field replaces, whole line, the one a @@trait supplies under the same name — a host tightening a reference trait's default or column name. |
| `@@sync` | in a model · in a trait | `(policy)` | This model's rows may be written with no server reachable: the client holds the write and replays it when one is. |
| `@@auth` | in a model · in a trait | — | This model is the principal auth() reads. |
| `@@person` | in a model · in a trait | `[(child)]` | Every row is a person — where forgetting and export start. |
| `@@mirror` | in a model · in a trait | `(key: <field>)` | The rows are a Provider's: a third party is the system of record, and the named column holds its id for each row. |
| `@@anonymous` | in a model · in a trait | — | No row of this model may be attributed. |
| `@@db` | in a model | `(<database>)` | Which declared database this model lives in. |
| `@@trait` | in a model · in a trait | `(<TraitName>)` | Splice a trait's fields and attributes in here. |
| `@@createdBy` | in a model · in a trait | `[(<base>)]` | The model-level form: declare the created-by column for this model without naming it on a field. |
| `@@updatedBy` | in a model · in a trait | `[(<base>)]` | The model-level form of @updatedBy. |

- `@@sync` **`policy`** takes `server` · `append` · `refuse` · `field` · `read`
